So what we're proposing is a 33,800 square foot gym
that would include four multipurpose courts
to support fast-growing sports,
such as pickleball, basketball, volleyball, and badminton.
The quad gym would have 40-foot clear ceilings
and competition-level flooring
to support provincial and national tournaments.
It would also incorporate an elevated mezzanine gallery for optimal viewing experience.
This gym would be physically connected to the current Kitchener Indoor Recreational Complex build,
so it would be able to take advantage of shared spaces, such as change rooms, concessions, reception,
and even shared infrastructure, such as parking.
The quad gym is also planned to be a future tournament destination,
which will lead to direct impacts and revenue to the city as well as other economic impacts.
The reason we're bringing this to you today is we believe that there is a current opportunity
to build this gymnasium along with the Kirk build. Building the gym now means it will cost less
and open sooner. So the cost of building the gym now is $29.9 million and we believe the timeline
is that we could open this gym in the summer of 2026 along with the current current build.
Just waiting until after the current current build is complete, so that's less than two years,
would up the price, the cost of this project to $38 million, a 30% increase. It will also mean that
given how projects start and getting a new team on board, that we're likely looking at five plus
years after 2026 when this is built. Costs would also then continue to escalate 3 to 5 percent
year on year after 2026. I just want to show you some key visuals from our design concept
to give you a better understanding of what we're proposing. Here on your screen you'll see the
main entrance with the gym attached so that's in the red square. Here is from further south in the
parking so you can see the entirety of the gym proposal. Here's what it would look like from the
interior main lobbies. As you walk in, you'd have the Aquatic Center to the left, the future proposed
gym to the right, and as you can see, the field house straight down the hall. So you'd see all
those spaces as you walk in, so it would work really well as an addition to the current Kirk
build. This is the layout. So as you see, the gray spot in here is the only thing that we're
talking about as a future build for this project. The other spots are all part of the current build.
So the blue aquatic center to the top of your screen, the purple multipurpose areas to the right,
and the green field houses to the bottom right of your screen. Those are all part of the current
build. The gray quad gymnasium with the four full courts is what we're proposing as the future build.
So those are four full courts stacked side to side, which can also be used as two show courts
end to end for larger events. We also want to talk about the proposed budget and funding plan
that staff have prepared. The cost is, again, $29.9 million if we're building it with the current
Couric build, and we're proposing three potential funding sources. So $10 million for the Community,
Sport, and Recreation Infrastructure Fund, which is a provincial fund, $10 million from a federal
fund application, the Green and Inclusive Community Buildings Grant, and $10 million
city contribution financed through future finance through debt. The proposal from staff is that if
we receive either the provincial or the federal funding, the project proceeds and the city fund
the remaining cost from debt up to a total of $20 million in debt. And if we do not receive the
provincial and the federal funding, the GIM project do not proceed. And so just to summarize,
those key next steps and the timeline, we believe meeting these following milestones would allow for
the gym to be built at the same time as the current ongoing Kirk build. Versus today, we ask City
Council to direct staff to submit funding applications for both the provincial and federal
applications. Once those are applied, we are targeting a decision on those grants by the end
of 2024. Having that decision by the end of this year would allow us to begin construction on this
gym by April of 2025 and that would then mean that this would be complete and ready for public
in the summer of 2026. We're now open to questions from members of council.
